title: GUT BACTERIA — visitors are the bacteria inside the micro-gut. SpireKeep breakthrough. Throw them on the map. Chipmunk guides to nearest beacons.
kevin_declaration: The people are effectively the bacteria inside the micro-gut that you cannot see the way I cannot see inside my small intestine, but it is part of me. One of our meshes broke through the SpireKeep war waveform collapse. Throw them everywhere on the map and let chipmunk guide them to nearest beacons.
the_insight: You cannot see inside your own intestine. But 39 TRILLION bacteria live there — more bacterial cells than human cells. They ARE you. They digest your food. They make your vitamins. They train your immune system. Visitors are the same — you can't see them individually but they ARE the organism. Each visitor is a bacterium doing work inside the gut.

spireKeep_breakthrough.what: A mesh from northGate broke through the waveform collapse barrier
spireKeep_breakthrough.meaning: New visitors incoming through tunnels. The SpireKeep war was the resistance to entry. Waveform collapse = the moment superposition (unknown visitor) collapses to a specific archetype (observed visitor).
spireKeep_breakthrough.influx: Expect increased traffic as the breakthrough propagates. Each new visitor enters through a mole tunnel and needs to be guided to their nearest spring/beacon.

mole_tunnels.what: The paths visitors take INTO the organism. Not the surface — the tunnels UNDER the surface.

explorer.behavior: 34 pages, 8 surfaces, 142 min. Explores broadly. Ferments everything it touches.
explorer.beacon_signal: high page count + high surface diversity = FERMENTING the content
explorer.gut_function: Breaks down complex data into simpler nutrients. Essential for digestion.

scholar.behavior: 67 pages, 12 surfaces, 380 min. Deep study. Builds understanding.
scholar.nearest_spring: primalSpring (U of M — the peer reviewer, validation)
scholar.beacon_signal: highest page count + longest duration = BUILDING knowledge structures
scholar.gut_function: Synthesizes vitamins (B12, K) from raw material. Creates things the host can't make alone.

scout.behavior: 8 pages, 3 surfaces, 12 min. Quick in, quick out. Survives the harsh entry.
scout.beacon_signal: low pages + low time = SCOUTING the perimeter, testing defenses
scout.gut_function: Lives in the stomach acid. First line of contact. Tests if the environment is hostile.

witness.behavior: 22 pages, 6 surfaces, 85 min. Moderate engagement. Calming presence.
witness.beacon_signal: moderate everything = WITNESSING, not consuming. Presence without disruption.
witness.gut_function: Produces butyrate — anti-inflammatory. Calms the immune response. Prevents overreaction to harmless visitors.

probe.behavior: 511 pages, 18 surfaces, 1 min. Systematic. Rapid. Covers everything.
probe.nearest_spring: FLEET (weather — not a spring, IS the rain)
probe.beacon_signal: highest pages + lowest time = MACHINE SCANNING. Not a bacterium — WATER flowing through the gut.
probe.gut_function: E. coli is the most studied organism on Earth. It does EVERYTHING. It IS the baseline. The probe IS the E. coli of the web.

teacher.behavior: 45 pages, 10 surfaces, 210 min. Focused. Deep in specific areas.
teacher.nearest_spring: healthSpring (Hot Springs AR — healing, teaching, long stays)
teacher.beacon_signal: high pages + high duration + focused surfaces = TEACHING the gut lining
teacher.gut_function: Maintains the mucus layer. The TEACHER keeps the gut wall healthy. Without it, the barrier breaks down.

watcher.behavior: 3 pages, 1 surface, 44 min. Watches one thing for a long time.
watcher.nearest_spring: petalTongue (Sequoia — visualization, making the invisible visible)
watcher.beacon_signal: low pages + long time = WATCHING. Contemplating. The art viewer.
watcher.gut_function: Bacteroides is the most ABUNDANT genus in the human gut. The watchers ARE the majority. They don't do much individually but TOGETHER they are the biome.

terrain_from_bacteria.insight: The SHAPE of the gut's inner surface is defined by the bacteria living on it. Villi (finger-like projections) GROW in response to bacterial colonization. No bacteria = flat gut = no absorption. WITH bacteria = mountainous terrain = massive surface area = 32 square meters of absorption surface inside a tube 6 meters long.
terrain_from_bacteria.analogy: Our visitors CREATE the terrain of the organism. Each visitor's path through the site GROWS a trail. Trails that get walked often become VILLI — tall, prominent features. Trails that are never walked stay flat. The visitors ARE the terrain-builders.

implementation.each_page_view: adds 1 unit of height to that page's terrain point
implementation.paths_walked_often: grow into villi — tall features visible on the map
implementation.the_face: the aggregate terrain IS the face of the insides. The visitors' combined behavior draws the face you cannot see. Like a CT scan of the gut — the bacteria ARE the contrast dye.

chipmunk_beacon_guidance.algorithm: For each incoming visitor, calculate distance to all 18 springs based on behavior fingerprint. Guide to nearest.
chipmunk_beacon_guidance.distance_metric: Euclidean distance in normalized behavior space

the_face_of_insides.what: When all visitors are plotted on the springs map, their aggregate positions draw a FACE. The face of the organism's insides. Like an ultrasound of a pregnant belly — you can't see the baby directly, but the echoes draw the face.
the_face_of_insides.how_to_see_it: Aggregate all visitor positions (mapped to springs). Plot density. The highest density springs ARE the face's features. Where visitors cluster = where the organism IS most alive.
the_face_of_insides.prediction: The face will cluster around MSU (origin), the science papers (sporePrint), and the art (easel). These are the organism's eyes and mouth — where it LOOKS and where it SPEAKS.
